outOfScope: Global scheduler, role registry or organization workflow graph.
Exactly-once event transport or transactional outbox as a correctness prerequisite.
Deployment, AcceptanceSnapshot or Product QA semantics.
Execution-policy or strategy selection inside the activation boundary.
constraints: Event or queue delivery is not lifecycle, claim or execution authority.
Activation is not strategy selection and is not obligation creation.
Queue, cursor and local backoff state are disposable and reconstructable from canonical work state.
A stale queued hint cannot resurrect invalidated work.
Frontend and Backend independence is governed by exact semantic dependencies, not global development stages.
A durable runtime such as Restate may host activation mechanics but cannot become organizational source of truth or hidden scheduler.
invariants: one domain outage must not block unrelated domain work
queued stale hints cannot resurrect invalidated work
architectureDecisions: DOMAIN_ACTIVATION is a domain-local level-triggered reconciler over canonical actionable work, not a scheduler.
Wake-up events, watches, polls and restart scans are latency hints only; every reconcile re-reads canonical work, owning-domain and obligation/currentness state before claim.
Activation keys are exact projectId/workId/owningDomain identities. Role, stage, queue position and trigger payload never grant claim or execution authority.
Canonical domain scans are the recovery source. Queue/cursor/backoff state is disposable and may be lost without stranding persisted actionable work.
Duplicate hints converge through the existing organization claim/release fencing plus DomainExecutionController attempt currentness; activation adds no exactly-once transport requirement.
Activation never resolves ExecutionStrategy and never creates obligations. It hands one current released claim to the existing domain-execution HOW boundary.

BB-052 is a hard execution dependency. The worker must consume its DONE consolidated Living truth and current obligation/currentness APIs; if the delivered dependency contradicts these plan assumptions, execution returns to RESEARCH_SA rather than adapting silently.

After activation pre-check and claim/release, the exact source obligation/currentness observation is revalidated immediately before domain execution entry. Drift invalidates/fences the organization claim and the stale hint becomes NOOP.

Backend receives a domain-local strategy adapter over existing Backend worker/application primitives; createDurableBackendQaWorkflow is not reused as the strategy because QA cross-domain control is outside this boundary.
Frontend becomes a first-class independent domain with explicit contract/result/context/completion semantics and its own strategy descriptor; FE and BE have no implicit global stage barrier.
A domain outage affects only that domain's reconciliation/execution loop. Unrelated owning domains continue discovering and executing their own actionable work.
DomainActivationObservation is telemetry only and cannot become lifecycle, claim, obligation, strategy or publication authority.

Frontend and Backend are composed as two independent domain runtimes. Each runtime binds exactly one owningDomain, one trusted domain principal, one DomainActivationController and one DomainExecutionController instance; no activation instance routes work to a different domain.

The Backend and Frontend DomainExecutionController instances may share canonical organization/execution stores, but each is bound to its own runtimeAdapter. Strategy authority remains the existing execution policy keyed by (owningDomain, workloadType); activation passes only the released claim subject and cannot choose the policy, strategyRef or runtime adapter.

Parallel progress means there is no control edge between unrelated FE and BE work. The acceptance fixture must hold both domain runtime dispatches behind independent barriers and prove both have entered their own execution attempt before either barrier is released; sequential completion after one domain finishes is not sufficient evidence.

FE/BE independence is evidenced by distinct workContractRef, executionPolicyRef, executionStrategyRef, executionAttemptId and runtimeInvocationKey for the two domains. Shared CAS/artifact stores arbitrate currentness only and are not a global stage lock.

The existing runBackendThenQaObjective composition is a legacy explicit serial Backend-to-QA flow and is not reused as Integration D activation/orchestration. Integration D introduces domain-runtime composition without a Backend-first or Frontend-first dispatcher.
implementationSlices: D1 — Activation source/controller [AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, INV-1, INV-2, INV-3]: add domain-activation-source.js with scan({owningDomain}) over canonical actionable OrganizationWork plus optional hint(workId), and domain-activation.js with reconcile(DomainActivationKey={projectId,workId,owningDomain}). reconcile re-reads exact work + owningDomain + BB-052 currentness, returns NOOP for absent/non-actionable/stale/wrong-domain subjects, and contains no list ranking, role transition or strategy lookup.

D2 — Claim/execution admission [AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, INV-1, INV-4, INV-5, INV-8]: DomainActivationController is constructed for exactly one owningDomain/trusted principal and an executeReleasedClaim entrypoint. For one current subject it uses existing organization claim/release authority, then re-observes the exact BB-052 obligation/currentness immediately before execution entry; mismatch invokes canonical claim invalidation/fencing and returns NOOP. On match it calls the prebuilt domain execution entrypoint with {itemId,claimGeneration,receiptRef} only—no policyRef, strategyRef, runtime adapter or publication decision is accepted from activation input.

D3 — Backend domain runtime [AC-5, AC-6, INV-4, INV-7]: add backend-execution-strategy.js implementing the DomainExecutionController runtimeAdapter contract {adapterRef,runtimeKind,runtimeDeploymentRef,producerAuthorityRef,dispatch,recover}. dispatch maps the exact Backend WorkContract into existing prepare/run Backend application primitives; recover maps to existing Backend recovery. Add no QA handoff or next-role action. domain-runtime-composition.js constructs a BACKEND activation/controller pair with BACKEND principal + Backend runtimeAdapter while the existing execution policy for (BACKEND, workloadType) remains sole strategyRef authority.

D4 — Frontend domain runtime [AC-5, AC-6, INV-6, INV-7]: add frontend-contracts.js, frontend-worker.js and frontend-application.js with explicit Frontend objective/order/context/result/recovery semantics, then frontend-execution-strategy.js implementing the same runtimeAdapter contract. domain-runtime-composition.js constructs a separate FRONTEND activation/controller pair with FRONTEND principal + Frontend runtimeAdapter. No Frontend API reads Backend completion/stage/session state; only its exact OrganizationWork semantic dependencies/currentness can block it.

D5 — Parallel autonomy proof [AC-5, AC-6, AC-7, INV-6, INV-7]: fe-be-parallel.test.js creates two unrelated actionable work items with distinct owningDomain/workloadType, active execution policies and strategy descriptors. It starts BACKEND and FRONTEND reconcile concurrently, blocks each runtime dispatch on its own deferred barrier, and asserts both dispatchStarted signals plus distinct workContractRef/executionPolicyRef/executionStrategyRef/executionAttemptId/runtimeInvocationKey before releasing either barrier. It then fails one domain adapter and proves the other reaches terminal/current progress without waiting for or mutating the failed domain.

D6 — Recovery/invalidation proof [AC-1, AC-2, AC-4, AC-8, INV-2, INV-8]: activation-recovery.test.js drops all hint/cursor state and proves canonical scan rediscovers work after restart; duplicate scan+event hints converge on the existing claim/attempt currentness. partial-invalidation.test.js supersedes one exact obligation between pre-check and execution entry and proves only that subject is fenced/NOOP while an unrelated domain subject remains executable. DomainActivationObservation records latency/outcome only and is never read as authority.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Persisted actionable work is rediscovered and processed after controller restart even when its original notification was lost.
evidenceRequired: Restart fixture drops the original hint, reconstructs from canonical scan, and enters one current claim/execution path.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Concurrent duplicate hints for one work item converge to one current claim/execution path.
evidenceRequired: Concurrent event+scan hints for the same exact work key produce one claim generation/current execution attempt; duplicates return NOOP/replay.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A wrong-domain activation attempt cannot claim or execute the work.
evidenceRequired: Wrong-domain controller/principal is rejected before executable claim or DomainExecutionController entry.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Obligation supersession between activation pre-check and execution entry prevents execution through the post-release currentness recheck.
evidenceRequired: Race fixture supersedes the exact source obligation after pre-check; post-release recheck fences the claim and no execution dispatch occurs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Frontend and Backend work can progress concurrently and independently under their own domain execution strategies.
evidenceRequired: fe-be-parallel fixture starts unrelated BACKEND and FRONTEND reconciles concurrently and holds each runtime dispatch on an independent barrier.

Before either barrier is released, evidence must show both domains reached dispatchStarted and have distinct current workContractRef, executionPolicyRef, executionStrategyRef, executionAttemptId and runtimeInvocationKey.
The fixture contains no Backend-first/Frontend-first stage variable or cross-domain next-role call; activation inputs contain no strategyRef/runtime adapter choice.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An outage in one domain leaves unrelated work in another domain actionable and able to progress.
evidenceRequired: With both domains independently actionable, inject a dispatch/recovery failure into one domain runtime and prove the unrelated domain still discovers, claims, dispatches and reaches its own current completion path.
The failed domain's attempt/claim state is not used as a prerequisite or lock by the progressing domain.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Removing a manual next-role dispatcher does not stop progress for persisted actionable work.
evidenceRequired: Fixture has no manual next-role dispatcher and still progresses persisted actionable FE/BE work from canonical reconciliation.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Partial upstream invalidation suppresses only affected activation subjects while unrelated domain work remains actionable.
evidenceRequired: Partial invalidation makes only affected activation subjects NOOP/fenced while unrelated work remains actionable and executes.
Negative case proves trigger/event payload fields cannot authorize claim, execution or publication.
Lost/deleted hint queue state followed by restart scan yields the same actionable work; queue/cursor deletion changes no canonical truth.
Activation API accepts exact work identities and exposes no role/stage ranking or next-work selection path.
Activation cannot supply/resolve an ExecutionStrategy; existing DomainExecutionController policy/strategy authority remains required.
Activation cannot create or mutate CrossDomainObligation; only current BB-052 obligation state may be consumed.
FE work is not blocked by unrelated Backend stage state; only explicit semantic dependencies affect actionability.

evidenceRequired: One-domain-down test proves unrelated domain progress continues.

evidenceRequired: Stale queued hint after selective invalidation cannot resurrect, claim or execute invalidated work.

negativeVerificationCases: An event payload that contains principal/domain/strategy fields cannot directly authorize claim, execution or publication.
A request to activate a BACKEND/FRONTEND role or workflow stage without an exact projectId/workId/owningDomain key is rejected.
A controller configured for the wrong owning domain cannot claim or execute the work.
Deleting or losing queue/cursor/hint state cannot strand canonical actionable work; restart scan rediscovers it.
Concurrent duplicate event and scan hints cannot create two current claim generations or two current execution attempts for one work item.
Activation cannot resolve, choose or override ExecutionStrategy; existing execution-policy authority remains mandatory.
Activation cannot create a CrossDomainObligation or make a non-current obligation current.
Frontend cannot be forced to wait for a whole Backend stage when its exact semantic dependencies are satisfied.
A stale queued hint after obligation/selective invalidation becomes NOOP/fenced and cannot resurrect executable capability.
A Backend activation outage cannot prevent unrelated Frontend work from being discovered and executed.
A supposedly parallel FE/BE test that starts Frontend only after Backend completion does not satisfy AC-5; both domain dispatches must be observed entered before either is released.
A single activation/controller instance that switches on owningDomain to choose Backend versus Frontend strategy/runtime is rejected as hidden cross-domain dispatch authority.
A shared global mutex/stage flag that blocks Frontend while Backend execution is active is rejected even if both domains eventually complete.
